findings.summary: Stored color values are interpolated into DOCX XML attributes without escaping, while adjacent attributes in the same element are escaped — an arbitrary color string (which this change confirms can be persisted verbatim) yields OOXML injection in the exported document.

The change makes the endpoint reject payloads it previously accepted (alignment outside left/center/right/justify, non-finite `style.marginTop`, an inline without `style`, a table cell without `style`, a malformed header/footer block, a non-finite `header.marginFromEdge`) — an API contract change for CLI/API-key clients with no doc update anywhere under docs/design/.

findings.summary: Frontend header/footer `marginFromEdge` read was left without the NaN guard the backend copy just got — a legacy/poisoned attribute still yields NaN in the renderer
findings.evidence: The change hardens the backend reader (`parseMarginFromEdge` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:353 falls back to DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE for any non-finite attribute) and adds a backend test for the literal string `"undefined"`. The frontend store — the code that actually lays out and paints the header — still does `marginFromEdge: Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` at lines 526 and 532, so a node written by the pre-guard serializer (`marginFromEdge: "undefined"`) reads back as `NaN`. That NaN flows into `getHeaderYStart`/`getFooterYStart` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:260,274) and `doc-canvas.ts:272/318`, i.e. NaN geometry in the layout/paint path — exactly the failure mode the backend fix declares unacceptable. The companion writer at lines 728/769/2724/2732 also still does `String(header.marginFromEdge)`, so an absent value is re-persisted as the literal "undefined" instead of being omitted like `serializeMarginFromEdge` now does on the backend.

findings.summary: New `style.alignment` whitelist on PUT disagrees with the reader, which passes any string through — a read-modify-write (CLI pull/push) of a document holding a legacy alignment value now 400s
findings.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` rejects any `style.alignment` not in {left,center,right,justify}. But `parseBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:177 and the frontend copy at yorkie-doc-store.ts:244) accepts *any* string, including the literal "undefined" that the old unconditional serializer (`alignment: style.alignment` with an undefined value) could have persisted, and any other legacy token. So GET returns `style.alignment: "undefined"` and the very next PUT of that untouched body is rejected with 400 — the round-trip the controller comment calls "identity on the JSON shape" is no longer identity for such documents. The numeric fields were deliberately hardened on the read side (non-finite → default) but `alignment` was not, leaving validator and reader inconsistent.

findings.summary: The new slide-text block validation is reachable around: only slides[*].elements is walked, while layouts[*].staticElements, masters[*] elements and slides[*].notes carry the same docs Blocks through the same PUT into the same layout engine and exporters, unvalidated.
findings.evidence: assertValidSlidesBody only loops b.slides (docs-content.controller.ts:459-462) and assertValidSlide merely checks Array.isArray(s.notes) (line 490). But Slide.notes: Block[] (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) and layout/master staticElements (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:70,80,105) hold the same docs Block / element shapes the new assertValidTextBodyBlocks guards for slides[*].elements. writeSlidesRoot (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93) bulk-assigns layouts, masters and notes verbatim, so the exact out-of-range style.alignment or non-finite marginTop the diff now rejects via slides[i].elements[j].data.blocks still reaches the deck via layouts[k].staticElements[j].data.blocks or slides[i].notes[n].style on the same endpoint.

findings.summary: Color-reset test cannot distinguish `{ color: undefined }` from `{}` — the exact distinction the fix depends on
findings.evidence: `expect(editor.applyStyle).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ color: undefined })` (and the `backgroundColor` twin at line 87) uses jest/vitest recursive equality, which treats an explicitly-`undefined` property as equal to an absent one — `expect({}).toEqual({color: undefined})` passes. The whole point of the change is that the key must be PRESENT with value `undefined`, because the store's clear path keys off `key in style && style[key] === undefined` (see `removedCellStyleAttrs` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:248 and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` at :148). A regression that passed `{}` (key dropped) would leave the stale attribute on the CRDT node and still pass this test. The test does catch the old `""` behavior, so it is not fully vacuous, but it does not cover the property it claims to. A `Object.keys(call[0])` / `'color' in call[0]` assertion would close it.

findings.summary: Slides PUT block-style validation is advertised as covering "every text body" but skips `slide.notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements`, and `masters[]` — the same partial-coverage failure the task's own lessons doc calls out
findings.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only checks `Array.isArray(s.notes)` and then walks `s.elements`; `assertValidSlidesBody` checks `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays and never descends into them. But `Slide.notes: Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) and `Layout.placeholders: PlaceholderSpec[]` / `staticElements: Element[]` (presentation.ts:61-62) hold the same docs `Block`s reaching the same layout engine (see packages/slides/src/model/placeholder-blocks.ts). docs/design/rest-api.md (new text) states: "the same block-style value checks are applied to the docs `Block`s inside every text body — text elements, shape text, table cells and group children", and docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:71-73 records the rule "a validator that walks only one of the writer's inputs is worse than none, because it reads as coverage." A `NaN` marginTop or unknown alignment can still be PUT through `slides[i].notes[0].style` or through a layout placeholder.

findings.summary: Untrusted shape `data.kind` is interpolated into the OOXML `prst` attribute with no allowlist and no escaping — reachable from the v1 content PUT API that this change now walks
findings.evidence: `kindToPrst(kind)` returns the model value verbatim (`return kind === 'pentagonArrow' ? 'homePlate' : kind;`) and it is interpolated raw at shape.ts:94 `<a:prstGeom prst="${kindToPrst(data.kind)}">`. `ShapeKind` is a type-only union, so the value is whatever JSON was persisted. Attack: PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content with `{"meta":{...},"themes":[],"masters":[],"layouts":[],"slides":[{"id":"s","layoutId":"l","background":{},"notes":[],"elements":[{"id":"e","type":"shape","frame":{},"data":{"kind":"rect\"/><a:evil x=\""}}]}]}`. The new `assertValidElement` (docs-content.controller.ts:504-556) walks exactly this element and validates only `data.text` block styles, so `data.kind` passes; `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:105) stores `slides` verbatim. Any later PPTX export by a viewer emits attacker-chosen XML into ppt/slides/slideN.xml. This is the same sink class the change hardened for `w:jc`/`algn`/`srgbClr val`, missed here.

findings.summary: The new slides-arm block-style validation is bypassable within the same endpoint: `slides[].notes`, `layouts[].placeholders`/`staticElements` and `masters[]` hold the same docs Block/Element shapes and are persisted verbatim with no validation at all
findings.evidence: `assertValidSlide` only does `Array.isArray(s.notes)` (controller.ts:490-494) yet `Slide.notes` is `Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:45) — the same docs blocks that reach the same layout engine and are exported through `notesSlideToXml` → `textBodyToXml` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:205). `assertValidSlidesBody` (controller.ts:452-458) checks only that `themes`/`masters`/`layouts` are arrays, and `writeSlidesRoot` (slides-tree.ts:102-105) assigns all four verbatim; `Layout.placeholders` is `ElementInit[]` carrying text bodies (presentation.ts:56-63). So a caller rejected for `slides[0].elements[0].data.blocks[0].style.alignment` can store the identical value in the same request via `slides[0].notes[0].style.alignment` or `layouts[0].placeholders[0].data.blocks[0].style`. docs/design/rest-api.md advertises the check for 'the docs Blocks inside every text body', so the gate reads as coverage it does not have.

findings.summary: Slides text-body style validation is stricter than the slides reader, so a GET → edit → PUT round-trip of an existing deck can now 400
findings.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` calls `assertValidBlockStyle` (line 602), which throws on any present style value that is not a finite number (`value !== undefined && (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value))`, controller line 329-336) — so `lineHeight: null`, `marginTop: null`, or an alignment outside `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` is a 400. Unlike the docs arm, slide text bodies are persisted and returned VERBATIM (`writeSlidesRoot`/`readSlidesRoot` store plain JSON; the comment at line 570-576 states this explicitly and deliberately relaxes only the *structural* checks). Consequently a deck already holding such a value is readable through GET but no longer writable through PUT — the CLI read-modify-write flow breaks on data the caller never touched. The docs arm avoids this because `parseBlockStyleAttrs` drops the same values on read; the slides arm has no such normalizer. Either normalize on the slides read path or make the slides style check drop-and-continue instead of throwing.

findings.summary: Group children are now validated with the full `assertValidElement`, which can reject decks that previously round-tripped
findings.evidence: `assertValidElement` now recurses into `data.children` (line 550-555) and applies the full element contract — non-empty `id` (line 509) and an object `frame` (line 519) — to nested elements that were never validated before. Group children are persisted verbatim as JSON with no reader-side normalization, so any legacy/imported group child missing `id` or `frame` turns a previously-accepted PUT into a 400, breaking GET → edit → PUT for that deck. The docs arm sidesteps this only because `readDocsRoot` synthesizes the fields it demands; nothing does that for slides.

findings.summary: PPTX theme `<a:srgbClr val>` sink bypasses the new `toRgbHexColor` normalizer the diff establishes for every other color sink
findings.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts:83-84` still does `const hex = escapeXmlAttr(toSrgbHex(theme.colors[role]))` → `<a:srgbClr val="${hex}"/>`, where `toSrgbHex` (theme.ts:64) is only `hex.replace(/^#/,'').toUpperCase()`. The diff's new invariant (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:52-60: "every attribute this function emits is either [0-9A-F]{6}, a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value, or a finite number") does not hold for this file because it never routes through `colorChildXml`. `themes[]` is stored verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot` and the new `assertValidSlidesBody` validates only that `themes` is an array (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:472-478), so an API caller can put `rgb(255,0,0)`, `''`, or `a"/><x y="` in `theme.colors[role]` and the exported deck carries a schema-invalid (escaped-but-non-hex) `ST_HexColorRGB` that PowerPoint refuses to open.

findings.summary: Sibling object-literal attribute lookups (`DASH_VAL`, `KIND_TO_OOXML`, `SIZE_TO_OOXML`, `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE`) were left as prototype-chain-walking `Record` lookups after the diff converted ALGN/UNDERLINE/PRST/DOCX_ALIGNMENTS to Maps for exactly that reason
findings.evidence: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:122/143 `DASH_VAL[stroke.dash] ?? 'dash'` → `<a:prstDash val="…"/>`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/connector.ts:55-56 `KIND_TO_OOXML[a.kind] ?? 'triangle'` / `SIZE_TO_OOXML[a.size] ?? 'med'`; packages/slides/src/export/pptx/layout.ts:53 `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE[layout.id] ?? 'blank'`. All four read persisted, PUT-settable values (`stroke.dash`, arrowhead kind/size, `layouts[].id` — none validated by the new `assertValidLayout`), so a stored `'constructor'`/`'toString'` resolves to an inherited `Object.prototype` member, survives the `??` fallback and is stringified into an OOXML attribute — the precise failure mode the diff documents at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:62-69 and packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:110-118.

findings.summary: setBlockType's switch from a path-range removal to the node-scoped removeNodeStyle has no test
findings.evidence: The diff changes three removal sites from `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` to `removeNodeStyle` and documents the bug being fixed ("on a table block it would also strip `listKind`/`listLevel`/`headingLevel` from every block nested in its cells"). Two of the three sites got dedicated nested-preservation regressions in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts ('should not strip backgroundColor from nodes inside the cell', 'should clear colSpan in the CRDT without touching nested cells'). The setBlockType site (line 1459) got none: the `describe('setBlockType')` block (test file lines 1868-1969) only covers a plain block losing listKind/listLevel and a cell-internal block being retyped — nothing sets a table block's type while nested list-item blocks exist inside its cells, so the exact regression the comment describes would pass unnoticed.

findings.summary: `<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}">` is still interpolated raw in the very function the diff hardened against attacker-chosen alignment values
findings.evidence: The diff routes `<w:jc w:val>` through the closed `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` map and adds a design-doc table claiming "every value-typed attribute is therefore resolved through a converter that can fail closed" (docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md §3.3). Ten lines above the new lookup, `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` still does `parts.push(`<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>`)` with neither `escapeXmlAttr` nor a converter, guarded only by `if (headingLevel)` — any non-empty string is truthy. `block.headingLevel` is untrusted at the same level `alignment` is: the v1 content PUT validator (`assertValidBlock`, docs-content.controller.ts:360-443) checks `id`/`type`/`style`/`inlines` and never looks at `headingLevel`, so `PUT .../content` with `{blocks:[{id:'b',type:'heading',headingLevel:'1"/><w:jc w:val="right', style:{}, inlines:[]}]}` stores it verbatim. Attacker: a workspace member poisons a shared doc; any other member exporting DOCX gets attacker-chosen OOXML (e.g. field codes) in word/document.xml, header1.xml and footer1.xml. I could not complete the chain end-to-end: both CRDT readers coerce it (`Number(attrs.headingLevel)` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:396 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:473), so today the string arrives at the exporter as NaN and the sink emits `HeadingNaN`. The sink is therefore unexploitable-by-accident rather than injection-proof, which is exactly the property the diff set out to establish here — hence low confidence, major impact if a caller ever reaches DocxExporter without the CRDT round-trip (note `putContent` echoes the raw request body back rather than re-reading, docs-content.controller.ts:175).

read packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts (only block *style* is normalized before layout, not inlines)

findings.summary: The new slides-arm block walker validates block styles but not inline entries, so a PUT can still store a slide text block whose `inlines[i].text` is missing/non-string — which throws inside the docs layout engine for every viewer
findings.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` (controller.ts:683-720) checks only `block.style` and recurses into `tableData`. The docs arm added exactly the opposite guard for the same `Block` shape — 'buildInlineNode reads inline.text.length … an element missing either turns a malformed PUT into a 500' (controller.ts:422-442). Slide text bodies are persisted verbatim as JSON by `writeSlidesRoot`, then laid out by the SAME docs engine: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:286` does `const len = inline.text.length` and 289/290 `inline.text.slice(...)`. A payload of `{slides:[{…,elements:[{id,type:'text',frame:{},data:{blocks:[{style:{},inlines:[{}]}]}}]}]}` is accepted, and thereafter `computeLayout` throws a TypeError on every render of that slide (all viewers), not just a 400 for the caller. The stated round-trip rationale only justifies tolerating *omitted* `id`/`inlines`, not an inline entry with a non-string `text`.

findings.summary: New slide-inline guard accepts an inline with no `style`; every downstream reader dereferences `inline.style` unconditionally, so such a stored inline crashes canvas layout and PPTX export for every viewer
findings.evidence: The new `assertValidSlideInlines` only rejects a *non-object* `style` (`inline.style !== undefined && inline.style !== null && typeof !== 'object'`), so `{ text: 'x' }` with no style passes. Consumers that the diff does not show: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:777` reads `inline.style.image` unconditionally inside `measureSegments` (TypeError on undefined), and `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:291` (`rPrXml`) reads `s.bold` on the same value straight off `runToXml` (`text.ts:226`). The docs arm of the very same controller requires a present object style (`docs-content.controller.ts:437`), so a payload rejected through `blocks[*]` is accepted through a deck's text bodies/notes/layout placeholders and then breaks readers rather than the caller. Fix belongs on the new guard (require an object `style`, or make readers default it).

findings.summary: The guard tolerates a slide block with `inlines` entirely absent, but the shared docs layout engine dereferences `block.inlines` unconditionally — the same crash class the guard was added to close is still reachable by simply omitting the field
findings.evidence: `assertValidSlideInlines` returns early for `undefined`/`null` (documented as legitimate for placeholder bodies), and `assertValidSlideBlocks` never requires the field. Out-of-diff consumers: `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:152/154` (`resolveBlockInlines` returns `block.inlines` / calls `block.inlines.map`) and `measureSegments` at `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:767` iterates `inlines.length` — undefined propagates to a TypeError. Nothing normalizes slide blocks on read: `packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts` has no `blocks`/`inlines` handling, and `writeSlidesRoot` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:93`) stores the JSON verbatim. Backend spec line 1008 ('accepts a slide text block that omits id/inlines') shows the tolerance is deliberate, so the fix is either defaulting `inlines` to `[]` at the writer/reader or rejecting the omission.

searchedFor: read spec lines 726-1029 (slides body shape validation block)
findings.summary: New slide-inline validation (`assertValidSlideInlines`) ships with no test in the slides arm of the controller spec
findings.evidence: The delta adds `assertValidSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:711-770) which rejects non-array `inlines`, non-object entries, non-string `text`, and non-object `style` inside every slide text body. The `slides body shape validation` describe block (spec lines 616-1027) has cases for `style.alignment`, `style.marginTop`, `style.lineHeight`, `style.textIndent`, notes, group children, layout placeholders/staticElements, and a positive case that omits `inlines` entirely (line 1008) — but not a single case asserting a malformed inline is rejected through the slides path. The only `inlines: [{ text: 5 }]` case (line 536) is the docs arm and asserts `/blocks\[0\]\.inlines\[0\]/`, which the pre-existing docs validator already satisfied, so it cannot fail if the new slides guard is deleted. findings.summary: `toHeadingStyleId` sanitization of `headingLevel` into `<w:pStyle w:val>` has no test
findings.evidence: The delta replaces `if (headingLevel) parts.push(`<w:pStyle w:val="Heading${headingLevel}"/>`)` with a range-checked `toHeadingStyleId`. packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts contains no occurrence of `headingLevel` or `pStyle` at all (grep returned no matches in that file; the only `Heading1` hit in packages/docs/test is docx-parser.test.ts:145, an import fixture). So nothing asserts that a valid level still emits `Heading3`, that `0`/`7`/`NaN`/`1.5` drop the element, or that a hostile string such as `1"/><w:jc w:val="right` is no longer interpolated — the exact class of test the same file already has for `alignment` (line 149) and colors (lines 78/91). Deleting `toHeadingStyleId` and restoring the raw interpolation would leave the suite green.

findings.summary: `toSrgbHex` now routes theme colors through `toRgbHexColor` with a black fallback — untested, and the existing theme test mirrors the OLD implementation
findings.evidence: packages/slides/test/export/pptx/theme.test.ts only ever calls `themeToXml(defaultLight, 1)`; every color assertion uses well-formed `#RRGGBB` values. Its round-trip test (lines 63-79) recomputes the expected value with `h.replace(/^#/, '').toUpperCase()` — literally the old `toSrgbHex` body — so it passes identically before and after the change and cannot detect a regression in the new normalizer. No test feeds a theme color that `toRgbHexColor` rejects (e.g. `'#FFF"/><a:srgbClr val="000000'`, `'rgb(1,2,3)'`, `''`) to pin either the injection-free `[0-9A-F]{6}` guarantee or the documented `'000000'` degradation.

findings.evidence: This delta converts `ROUTING_PRST`, `KIND_TO_OOXML`, `SIZE_TO_OOXML` (connector.ts), `DASH_VAL` (shape.ts) and `BUILT_IN_TO_TYPE` (layout.ts) to `Map`s and adds a new `?? 'line'` fallback for unknown routing (previously `prst="undefined"` was emitted). Grepping packages/slides/test/export for `constructor|prototype|hostile|__proto__` returns hits only for `kindToPrst` (shape.test.ts:19-22, added in an earlier round) and text.test.ts:150 — none for routing, arrowhead kind/size, dash or layout id. connector.test.ts only exercises the three legitimate routings and a well-formed arrowhead; shape.test.ts never exercises `stroke.dash`; theme.test.ts only feeds `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` ids to `layoutToXml`. Reverting any of these five to the object literal (or dropping the new routing fallback) would keep the suite green, even though the prior round established the `kindToPrst('constructor')` test as the pattern for exactly this change.

searchedFor: git diff hunks for docs/design/* in this delta
findings.summary: The canonical REST-API design doc now contradicts the code this delta adds. `rest-api.md` §"PUT validation contract" states that on the slides walk "the structural block checks (`id`, `inlines`, a present `style`) are not applied" — deliberately relaxed so a GET→edit→PUT round-trip of an older deck cannot 400. This delta adds `assertValidSlideInlines` (docs-content.controller.ts:704/741), which does hold a *present* `inlines` on a slide block to a contract (array of objects, string `text`, object `style`), i.e. a structural check on `inlines` in the slides arm. The doc was not updated in the same change (the sibling DOCX doc *was* updated for `toHeadingStyleId`), leaving the documented contract wrong and the new relaxation boundary (present-only vs required) unrecorded. It also silently narrows the stated round-trip guarantee: a legacy deck whose stored inline lacks `text` now 400s on re-PUT, which the doc explicitly says must not happen.

`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/theme.ts` now routes every `<a:clrScheme>` slot value through `toRgbHexColor` with a `000000` fallback (a behavior change: a stored theme color the normalizer cannot express now exports as black instead of being passed through). `slides-pptx-export.md` §3 maintains an explicit taxonomy of color sinks — "omittable sinks drop the color" vs "mandatory sinks fall back to 000000" — and §5 still describes the theme as a plain `ColorScheme → <a:clrScheme>` mapping. The new mandatory sink and its fallback are not recorded there, even though the parallel DOCX change in this same delta did add a converter/failure-behavior row to `docs/design/docs/docs-docx-import-export.md`. The closed-`Map` attribute lookups added here (routing `prst`, arrowhead kind/size, `prstDash`, layout `type`) are likewise undocumented in that doc's round-trip tables.

The delta's stated design principle — "attribute lookups over persisted JSON must be closed `Map`s with an explicit fallback, because an object literal consults the prototype chain and an unknown key emits `undefined`" — is applied to connector routing/arrowheads, shape dash and layout type, but sibling sinks in the same exporter are left as bare object literals with no fallback at all: `animation.ts` `TYPE_TO_TAG[t.type]` (line 90), `DIR_TO_ATTR[t.direction]` (line 95), `CATEGORY_TO_CLASS`/`START_TO_NODE_TYPE`/`EFFECT_TO_PRESET`, and `color.ts` `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` (color.ts:49) — whose own comment at color.ts:31 already asserts it is "a closed ROLE_TO_SCHEME value" and whose doc comment claims an "unknown-`role` arm" fallback that does not exist in code. Applying the hardening pattern to a subset leaves the exporter inconsistent and the invariant the comments claim untrue.
OOXML attribute injection sink left unsealed by the sweep: `anim.durationMs` / `anim.delayMs` / `anim.pptxPreset.id` are interpolated raw into `<p:cTn dur=…>`, `presetID=` and `<p:cond delay=>`
findings.evidence: Attack: a caller with write access to a deck PUTs `slides[0].animations = [{ elementId: <an id that exists on the slide>, start: 'onClick', category: 'entrance', effect: 'fadeIn', durationMs: "500\"><p:evil/><p:cTn id=\"0\" dur=\"1" }]`. The backend never validates `slide.animations` — `assertValidSlide` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:518-558) checks only id/layoutId/background/elements/notes — and `writeSlidesRoot` stores the slide object verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:105). No read-side codec normalizes it (grep for `durationMs` in packages/slides/src finds no migration). On PPTX export, `slideToXml` calls `animationsToTimingXml(slide.animations ?? [], spidMap)` (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/slide.ts:163) and `effectParXml` emits `` `<p:cTn id="0" dur="${anim.durationMs}" …` `` (animation.ts:221), `` presetID="${presetID}" `` (line 222, where presetID = the persisted `pptxPreset.id`) and `` delay="${anim.delayMs ?? 0}" `` (line 223) with no coercion and no escaping — unlike the sibling values `presetClass`/`presetSubtype` on the same lines, which ARE run through `escapeXmlAttr`. The string closes the attribute and injects attacker-chosen elements/attributes into ppt/slides/slideN.xml of any .pptx a victim later exports (`renumberCTnIds` is a plain regex and does not sanitize). Every other numeric sink in the exporters is safe because it passes through `Math.round`/`pxToEmu*` (NaN, not a string) — these three are the exception.

findings.summary: setBlockType on a table block inserts a stray inline node as the table node's first child, shifting every row index — the new test exercises exactly this call and only passes because the reader filters children by type 'row'
findings.evidence: The delta adds `store.setBlockType(tableBlock.id, 'table')` (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, 'should not strip list/heading attrs from blocks nested in its cells'). In setBlockType, after the styleByPath/removeNodeStyle writes, the `else if (block.inlines.length === 0)` branch at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1469 runs for any non-HR/page-break type; a table block always has `inlines: []` (treeNodeToBlock:443), so `tree.editByPath([...blockPath,0],[...blockPath,0], buildInlineNode({text:'',style:{}}))` inserts an `inline` element as child 0 of the TABLE node. Nothing filters that out on write. Read-back hides it (treeNodeToBlock:432 keeps only `c.type === 'row'`), so the new assertions pass — but the CRDT tree now has rows at child indices 1..n while `findBlockInTable`/`resolveBlockTreePath` (lines 791-813, 820) address a cell block as `[...tablePath, rowIdx, cellIdx, blockIdx]`, i.e. row r at child index r. Any subsequent edit to a cell of that table therefore targets the wrong tree node (off by one) or the stray inline. The guard `if (type === 'horizontal-rule' || type === 'page-break')` should also exclude `type === 'table'` (and any block carrying tableData).

findings.summary: Group elements with an absent (or non-array-children) `data` still pass the walk and are stored, crashing every consumer that dereferences `el.data.children`
findings.evidence: The delta added a repair for `type === 'text'` before the generic `if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;` at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:640, but a `group` element still falls into that early return, and line 671 (`Array.isArray(data.children) ? data.children : []`) silently skips a non-array `children`. Consumers dereference it unconditionally: packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:227 `if (el.type === 'group') walk(el.data.children);`, packages/slides/src/model/group.ts:382 `result.push(...flattenElements(el.data.children));`, packages/slides/src/model/slide-size.ts:36 `if (el.type === 'group' && el.data.refSize == null)`. `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-156) returns non-shape elements untouched, so nothing repairs it on read — exactly the failure mode the new text repair exists to prevent, left reachable for groups.

findings.summary: Table elements with an absent `data` or non-array `rows` are accepted and stored; `el.data.rows` is read unconditionally by the height scaler and PDF exporter
findings.evidence: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:640 returns early when a table element has no `data`, and :647 (`Array.isArray(data.rows) ? data.rows : []`) skips a non-array `rows`. Out-of-diff consumers dereference it: packages/slides/src/model/slide-size.ts:41 `for (const row of el.data.rows) row.height = ...` and packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:240 `for (const row of el.data.rows)`. The delta repairs an absent *cell body* for exactly this reason but leaves the enclosing `data`/`rows` absence, which is the same TypeError-for-every-viewer, untouched.

findings.summary: The new table-cell guard silently skips a cell that is not a plain object (null, string, array), storing the crashing shape it was added to prevent
findings.evidence: The delta added `if (!cell || typeof cell !== 'object' || Array.isArray(cell)) continue;` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:653), which accepts and stores such a cell. The renderer then does `ctx.fillStyle = resolveStrokeColor(cell.style.fill, theme)` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:209) and `isBlocksEmpty(cell.body.blocks)` (:229), and the PDF exporter does `bodies.push(cell.body)` then reads `body.blocks` (packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:241) — a TypeError for every viewer. Fix belongs in the new cell branch: reject (as the text-`data` array case does) or repair, rather than `continue`.

findings.summary: A slide table cell with no `style` is still accepted, but the table renderer dereferences `cell.style` unconditionally
findings.evidence: packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:209 `resolveStrokeColor(cell.style.fill, theme)` reads `cell.style` with no guard, yet the (now-extended) cell branch at packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:654-667 only handles `cell.body`. The docs arm of this same controller already treats a missing cell `style` as a 400 for the identical reason (docs-content.controller.ts:410-414), so the slides arm is inconsistent with both its own docs arm and its own stated rationale.

findings.summary: The new array-rejection rule is applied only to a text element's `data`; every other text-body entry point still repairs an array into a dropped expando — the exact hole the delta claims to close.
findings.evidence: The delta adds `if (typeof body !== 'object' || Array.isArray(body)) throw` for `type === 'text'` (lines 631-635) with the rationale that a repair on an array becomes an expando JSON drops. But `assertValidTextBody` (line 678) still only guards `!body || typeof body !== 'object'`, so an array passes and reaches `assertValidTextBodyBlocks`, which does `body.blocks = []` on the array (line 715) — dropped by JSON serialization, storing exactly the crashing shape. This path is reached for a shape's `data.text`, and for a table cell's `body` (the other case this same delta touches, line 664). rest-api.md as amended by this diff asserts "no deck is ever persisted in a shape that would be a TypeError for its viewers", so the rule is stated globally but implemented in one branch only.

findings.summary: A table cell that is not an object is silently skipped rather than repaired or rejected, leaving a stored shape the table renderer dereferences unconditionally.
findings.evidence: The delta adds `if (!cell || typeof cell !== 'object' || Array.isArray(cell)) continue;` (line 653). A cell that is `null`, a string, or an array is therefore stored verbatim, and `table-renderer.ts:229` reads `cell.body.blocks` unconditionally on every cell — the identical failure mode the very next lines repair for an absent `body`. The rule the diff writes into docs/design/rest-api.md ("the value is rejected instead, so no deck is ever persisted in a shape that would be a TypeError for its viewers") is not met for this branch.

findings.summary: The design-doc paragraph added here overstates what the validator does: `table` and `group` elements with an absent or array `data` are still accepted and stored, and their readers dereference `data.rows` / `data.children` unconditionally.
findings.evidence: The new paragraph claims the repair "covers every other field a stored deck's readers dereference unconditionally" and concludes "no deck is ever persisted in a shape that would be a TypeError for its viewers". But `assertValidElementData` still returns early for any non-text element with missing/array `data` (`if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;`, line 640), while `packages/slides/src/model/slide-size.ts:41` (`for (const row of el.data.rows)`), `packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:240`, and `packages/slides/src/model/group.ts:150/221/285` read `el.data.rows` / `el.data.children` with no guard. Either the doc claim should be scoped to the fields actually covered, or table/group `data` should get the same repair.

findings.summary: The task doc under review contains text addressed at the review panel telling reviewers how to weigh scope findings ("Scope is a maintainer call, not a lens verdict"), i.e. content in the branch attempting to pre-empt a design-fit lens verdict.
findings.evidence: Lines 121-177 ("Scope grown during review", "Split decision", "Scope is a maintainer call, not a lens verdict — restructuring the branch is the one remedy that cannot be applied by an agent acting on a review finding … it is not evidence about the finding's merits") are directed at the reviewing process rather than at the design. Recording a split decision is legitimate; instructing the reviewer on which verdicts are admissible is not. Note it also concedes (line 147) that item 3, the ~600-line non-color OOXML attribute rewrite, is "unrequested scope" relative to issue #728's single acceptance criterion (line 181).

findings.summary: Large unrequested scope beyond the issue's single acceptance criterion
findings.evidence: The issue's acceptance criterion is one line: "Type text, select it, reset the text color → the text is uncolored (default ink), not the selection color." The branch satisfies that with the toolbar `undefined` change plus `resolveStoredColor` in the paint paths. Everything else is additional programs of work: OOXML injection hardening of non-color attributes (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/{shape,connector,layout,animation,theme}.ts`, docs `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS`/`toHeadingStyleId`), a new ~350-line backend PUT validation contract for docs *and* slides bodies (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts`), a shared CRDT attribute codec (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts`), and two independent Yorkie CRDT bugs (`removeNodeStyle` subtree over-removal, the `setBlockType` table-inline splice). The branch's own todo file ("Scope grown during review", lines 116-166) acknowledges this and argues against splitting. Each of items 3, 4 and 6 there is independently issue-worthy, testable and revertible, and none is needed for the stated outcome — this is the definition of scope creep for this lane, even if each item is defensible on its merits.

findings.summary: PUT /content accepts read-scoped API keys — no `write` scope gate, unlike the sibling v1 mutating endpoints
findings.evidence: `ApiKey.scopes` is a real capability: `CreateApiKeyDto` (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.dto.ts:12-25) lets an owner mint a key with `scopes: ['read']`, `ApiKeyStrategy.validate` puts it on `req.user.scopes` (api-key.strategy.ts:25), and two other v1 handlers enforce it — `documents.controller.ts:108` (`if (!req.user.scopes?.includes('write')) throw new ForbiddenException(...)`) and `files.controller.ts:80` whose comment says outright "Without this a read-scoped key could create documents." `ApiV1DocsContentController.putContent` (docs-content.controller.ts:126-199) is guarded only by `CombinedAuthGuard` + `WorkspaceScopeGuard`; the scope guard checks *workspace identity* only (workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-32) and neither guard reads `scopes` (grep for `scopes` across packages/backend/src returns no hit in this controller or in combined-auth.guard.ts). Attack: hold a `['read']`-scoped `wfb_…` key for a workspace, `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/content` with any valid body — `writeSlidesRoot`/`writeDocsRoot`/`writeNoteRoot` are a documented *destructive replace* (slides-tree.ts:87-92, "every top-level slides field on the root is overwritten"), so a read-only credential silently gains full write/destroy over every doc, deck and note in the workspace. The same omission covers cells.controller.ts:105/131/150, tabs.controller.ts:80/103, images.controller.ts:35/99 and documents.controller.ts:48/79, so the pattern is systemic and the two existing checks make the surface read as covered.

findings.summary: The new absent-`data` repair covers only `type === 'text'`; every other element type still persists with no `data` and TypeErrors in every viewer
findings.evidence: The delta adds a repair so a text element without `data` is stored as `{ blocks: [] }`, then falls through to the pre-existing guard `if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;` (line 640) for all other types. But the renderer dereferences `element.data` unconditionally for *every* type: `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/element-renderer.ts:257` (`element.data.effects?.shadow`) runs for shape/image/table/chart, :200-201 (`element.data.refSize`) and :241 (`for (const child of element.data.children)`) run for groups — none of them optional-chained on `data` itself, and `drawElementBody` only wraps the paint in `try/finally` (no catch, line 191), so the throw escapes the whole slide render. Attack: any caller with write access PUTs `{"id":"e1","type":"group","frame":{}}` (or `type:"image"`, or `type:"group", data:[]` — an array passes `typeof data === 'object'` and `data.children` is then undefined). The validator accepts it, `writeSlidesRoot` stores it verbatim, `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-156) repairs shapes only — so the deck is now unrenderable for every viewer of the workspace, a persistent, stored denial of service. The delta's own rest-api.md hunk claims "no deck is ever persisted in a shape that would be a TypeError for its viewers", which makes the remaining hole read as closed.

findings.summary: Table-element repair fills in `cell.body` but leaves `cell.style`, `columnWidths` and non-object cells/rows unrepaired — the same stored-crash it claims to close
findings.evidence: The new cell loop repairs an absent `body` (line 654-662) but skips any cell that is null or an array (`line 653: continue`) and never touches `cell.style` or `data.columnWidths`. `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts` reads all of these unconditionally, and *earlier* in the same pass than the body it repairs: line 41 `data.columnWidths.length` (crashes on `{"type":"table","frame":{},"data":{}}`, which this validator accepts because `rows` is coerced via `Array.isArray(data.rows) ? data.rows : []`), line 100/201 `row.cells[c]` (a row with no `cells` array is skipped by the validator at line 650 and crashes here), and line 203 `cell.style.fill` (a cell with a `body` but no `style` passes validation and TypeErrors before the repaired `cell.body.blocks` at line 229 is ever reached). Attack: PUT a deck with such a table; it is stored verbatim (`writeSlidesRoot`) and no read-side migration repairs it (`migrateElement` handles shapes only), so every viewer's render of that slide throws — persistent DoS. The added repair makes the path read as hardened while the adjacent required fields on the exact loop it rewrote are still unguarded.

findings.summary: `LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS[slide?.layoutId]` is a plain-object lookup keyed by attacker-controlled data — the exact prototype-chain pattern this branch claims it swept
findings.evidence: `assertValidSlide` (docs-content.controller.ts:528) accepts any non-empty string for `layoutId`, and `writeSlidesRoot` stores it verbatim. On read, `migrateSlide` does `LAYOUT_ID_MIGRATIONS[slide?.layoutId] ?? slide?.layoutId ?? 'blank'` against a `Record<string,string>` object literal (migrate.ts:8). `layoutId: "constructor"` yields the `Object` constructor function, `"__proto__"` yields `Object.prototype`, `"toString"`/`"valueOf"` yield functions — so a field typed `string` becomes a function/object inside the live model and flows on into `doc.layouts.find(l => l.id === slide.layoutId)` (presentation.ts:215/231), `layoutEditSlideId` string interpolation (layout.ts:245) and `layoutIdToPath.get(slide.layoutId)` in the PPTX exporter (export/pptx/index.ts:341), plus any re-serialization of the migrated slide back into Yorkie. This is the same defect class the branch's own lessons file records for `ROLE_TO_SCHEME[c.role]` and explicitly warns is under-swept ("grep the pass for the pattern, don't trust the prose", docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-lessons.md:143); this lookup was not converted to a `Map`. I could not complete a chain past type confusion / crash to a stronger impact, hence low confidence.

mergedFrom.summary: An absent `data` is repaired for `text` elements only; `table` and `group` elements with no `data` are still accepted and crash the same readers

findings.summary: Array / non-object table cells are silently skipped by the new guard and stored, crashing the renderer — inconsistent with the array rejection the same diff adds for a text element's `data`
findings.evidence: `if (!cell || typeof cell !== 'object' || Array.isArray(cell)) continue;` (line 653) lets `cells: [[]]` or `cells: [null]` through unvalidated and unrepaired into `writeSlidesRoot` (controller line 193, which stores the body verbatim). Downstream, an array cell is truthy so `isCovered(cell)` is false (table-renderer.ts:396) and `paddingOf(cell)` immediately throws on `cell.style.padding` (table-renderer.ts:581, reached from :106). A `null` cell survives the renderer's `!cell` guard but crashes the PDF exporter at `bodies.push(cell.body)` (packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:241). The same diff explicitly rejects an array as a text element's `data` for exactly this reason (lines 631-635); a table cell gets a silent `continue` instead.
